intro: Hi! In the last lesson you made clauses shorter: the man standing there, the report written by Rina. Today you use the same -ing and V3 forms at the start of a sentence to write shorter, smoother sentences: Walking home, I saw Rina. Built in 1990, the bridge is still strong. Having finished the report, I went home. Warm-up: what's wrong with 'Walking home, the rain started'?
teachingNotes: Recap in one line from b2-relative-clauses-advanced (don't re-teach it): who/which + be can be dropped, leaving -ing (the man standing there = who is standing) or the V3 with a passive meaning (the report written by Rina = which was written). New here: a participle clause (klausa partisip) is a short part of a sentence with no subject and no tense, built on an -ing form, a V3 or having + V3, usually at the START of a sentence with a comma: Walking home, I saw Rina. It replaces when/while/because/after + subject + verb. The tense comes from the main clause (Walking home, I saw Rina = past; Walking home, I often listen to podcasts = present). Explain 'clause' (bagian kalimat dengan kata kerja), 'subject' (siapa yang melakukan) and 'participle' (bentuk -ing atau V3 dari kata kerja) the first time.

THE key rule (common error 1, the dangling participle): the subject of the main clause, the first noun or pronoun after the comma, must be the one doing the -ing action (or receiving the V3 action). *Walking home, the rain started (the rain wasn't walking) → Walking home, I got caught in the rain / As I was walking home, it started to rain. Indonesian trap: Indonesian is loose here ('Sambil berjalan pulang, hujan turun' or 'Setelah membaca surat itu, hatinya sedih' sound acceptable to many speakers), so learners carry it over. Test this with clear MCQ / A-B choices where only one ending has the right doer; a missing subject match is the most important thing to correct.

-ing clauses (objective ing-clauses): (1) same time = when/while + past continuous or present: Walking home, I saw Rina (= When I was walking home); (2) reason = because/as: Feeling tired, she went to bed early (= Because she felt tired); Knowing the area well, Budi took a shortcut. Negative: Not + -ing (Not knowing the way, we used Google Maps), never *Don't knowing / *No knowing. -ed clauses (objective ed-clauses): the V3 has a PASSIVE meaning and describes the subject of the main clause: Built in 1990, the bridge is still strong (= The bridge was built in 1990 and is still strong). Bridge to Indonesian: -ing ≈ me- (the subject does it), V3 ≈ di- (it is done to the subject: dibangun → built). Common error 2: the base form or past simple instead of the V3: *Build in 1990 → Built; *Took in 2019 → Taken (Indonesian verbs don't change form, so learners skip the V3). The -ed clause also needs the right subject: *Built in 1990, we still use the bridge.

having + V3 (objective having-past-participle) = an action that was finished BEFORE the main action, often over a period: Having finished the report, I went home (= After I had finished / After I finished). Negative: Not having received a reply, I called again. after / before / when / while + -ing (met at B1 as preposition + -ing): After finishing the report, I went home; Before leaving, turn off the AC. Common error 3: *After finish the report / *After finished → After finishing (or a full clause: After I finished the report). Both 'After finishing' and 'Having finished' are correct for an earlier action, and for quick actions one right after the other plain -ing is also used (Opening the email, Rina saw the bad news): NEVER make -ing vs having + V3 or After + -ing vs Having + V3 an either-or question. Test the FORM (Having signed vs Have signed / Having sign; after signing vs after sign / signed) and the subject match, with clear sentences.

Register: participle clauses are mostly WRITTEN and formal or semi-formal (reports, news, essays, CVs, emails, prepared presentations). In everyday speech people usually use full clauses: When I was walking home, I saw Rina. / I felt tired, so I went to bed early. / After I finished the report, I went home. Say this clearly; a learner who answers a free question with a correct full clause is right unless the question asks for a participle clause. Participle clauses can also come after the main clause (Sari sat on the KRL, reading the news) or after the subject: accept them, but teach and test the start-of-sentence position. Spelling: British practise / American practice; both accepted.

Limits: don't teach being + adjective clauses (Being tired, …: accept it if used correctly, but teach Feeling tired), result clauses (…, causing long delays), perfect passive (Having been told …), with + object + -ing (With prices rising, …), or fixed phrases like Generally speaking / Judging by. No third conditional, wish, causative, past modals or future perfect. Grammar allowed: A0–B1, b2-relative-clauses-advanced (non-defining and reduced relatives) and this lesson. Contexts: offices, campuses, KRL/MRT, ojek online, Bandung/Jakarta/Surabaya, news and reports.

keyPoints.title: -ing clauses: same time or reason
keyPoints.explanation: Start a sentence with an -ing clause to say what someone was doing at the same time, or why they did something: Walking home, I saw Rina (= When I was walking home). Feeling tired, she went to bed early (= Because she felt tired). The person after the comma must be the one doing the -ing action: 'Walking home, the rain started' is wrong, because the rain wasn't walking. This style is mostly for writing; in speech people usually say the full clause.

examples.id: Karena merasa lelah, dia tidur lebih awal.

id.title: Klausa -ing: bersamaan atau alasan
id.explanation: Awali kalimat dengan klausa -ing untuk mengatakan apa yang sedang dilakukan seseorang pada saat yang sama, atau kenapa dia melakukan sesuatu: Walking home, I saw Rina (= When I was walking home). Feeling tired, she went to bed early (= Because she felt tired). Orang setelah koma harus yang melakukan kegiatan -ing itu: 'Walking home, the rain started' salah, karena hujan tidak berjalan. Gaya ini terutama untuk tulisan; saat bicara orang biasanya memakai klausa lengkap.

keyPoints.title: -ed clauses: a passive meaning
keyPoints.explanation: Start with the third form (V3) when something is done TO the subject, like di- in Indonesian: Built in 1990, the bridge is still strong (= The bridge was built in 1990). Use the V3, not the base form: 'Build in 1990' is wrong. The subject after the comma must be the thing that received the action.

examples.en: Built in 1990, the bridge is still strong.
examples.id: Dibangun tahun 1990, jembatan itu masih kokoh.

examples.en: Written in simple English, the guide is easy to follow.
examples.id: Ditulis dalam bahasa Inggris sederhana, panduan itu mudah diikuti.

id.title: Klausa -ed: bermakna pasif
id.explanation: Awali dengan bentuk ketiga (V3) kalau sesuatu dikenai tindakan, seperti di- dalam bahasa Indonesia: Built in 1990, the bridge is still strong (= The bridge was built in 1990). Pakai V3, bukan bentuk dasar: 'Build in 1990' salah. Subjek setelah koma harus benda yang dikenai tindakan itu.

keyPoints.title: having + V3 and after + -ing: an earlier action
keyPoints.explanation: having + V3 shows that one action was finished before the next one: Having finished the report, I went home. You can also say After finishing the report, I went home. After before, after, when and while, use the -ing form, never the base form: 'After finish the report' is wrong.

id.explanation: having + V3 menunjukkan bahwa satu kegiatan sudah selesai sebelum kegiatan berikutnya: Having finished the report, I went home. Kamu juga bisa bilang After finishing the report, I went home. Setelah before, after, when dan while, pakai bentuk -ing, bukan bentuk dasar: 'After finish the report' salah.

material.title: From shorter clauses to participle clauses

blocks.text:
In the last lesson you made relative clauses shorter: *the man **standing** there* (= who is standing), *the report **written** by Rina* (= which was written).
Now the same forms go at the **start of a sentence**, followed by a comma. This is a **participle clause** (klausa partisip). A **participle** is the **-ing** form or the **third form (V3)** of a verb; a **clause** is a part of a sentence built around a verb. A participle clause has **no subject** and **no tense** of its own: it borrows them from the main part of the sentence.
An **-ing clause** can mean two things:
- **at the same time** (= when / while): *Walking home, I saw Rina.* = *When I was walking home, I saw Rina.*
- **a reason** (= because / as): *Feeling tired, she went to bed early.* = *Because she felt tired, she went to bed early.*
The time comes from the main clause: *Walking home, I **saw** Rina* is past; *Walking home, I often **listen** to podcasts* is present.
**Negative:** put **not** before the -ing: *Not knowing the way, we used Google Maps* (not *'Don't knowing'*).

id.text:
Di pelajaran sebelumnya kamu meringkas relative clause: *the man **standing** there* (= who is standing), *the report **written** by Rina* (= which was written).
Sekarang bentuk yang sama diletakkan di **awal kalimat**, diikuti koma. Ini disebut **participle clause** (klausa partisip). **Participle** (partisip) adalah bentuk **-ing** atau **bentuk ketiga (V3)** dari kata kerja; **clause** (klausa) adalah bagian kalimat yang punya kata kerja. Klausa partisip **tidak punya subjek** dan **tidak punya tense** sendiri: keduanya 'dipinjam' dari bagian utama kalimat.
**Klausa -ing** bisa berarti dua hal:
- **pada saat yang sama** (= when / while, saat / sambil): *Walking home, I saw Rina.* = *When I was walking home, I saw Rina.*
- **alasan** (= because / as, karena): *Feeling tired, she went to bed early.* = *Because she felt tired, she went to bed early.*
Waktunya ditentukan oleh klausa utama: *Walking home, I **saw** Rina* berarti lampau; *Walking home, I often **listen** to podcasts* berarti sekarang (kebiasaan).
**Bentuk negatif:** taruh **not** sebelum -ing: *Not knowing the way, we used Google Maps* (bukan *'Don't knowing'*).

blocks.text: **Writing vs speaking:** participle clauses are mostly used in **writing** (reports, news, essays, CVs, work emails) and prepared presentations. In everyday conversation, people usually say the full version: *When I was walking home, I saw Rina. / I felt tired, so I went to bed early.* Both are correct; the short one just sounds more written.

id.text: **Tulisan vs percakapan:** klausa partisip terutama dipakai dalam **tulisan** (laporan, berita, esai, CV, email kantor) dan presentasi yang disiapkan. Dalam percakapan sehari-hari, orang biasanya memakai versi lengkap: *When I was walking home, I saw Rina. / I felt tired, so I went to bed early.* Keduanya benar; versi pendek hanya terdengar lebih 'tulisan'.

blocks.prompt: What does this sentence mean? Hearing a strange noise, Dimas opened the door.

Dimas opened the door because he heard a strange noise.
blocks.explain: The -ing clause gives the reason: he heard a noise, so he opened the door. The person doing both actions is Dimas, the subject after the comma.

id.title: Dari klausa ringkas ke klausa partisip

material.title: The big rule: who is doing it?

blocks.text:
A participle clause has no subject, so English takes the subject from the main clause: the **first noun or pronoun after the comma** must be the one doing the -ing action.
- *Walking home, **I** got caught in the rain.* ✓ (I was walking)
- *Walking home, **the rain** started.* ✗ This says **the rain** was walking home!
If the doers are different, use a full clause instead: *As I was walking home, it started to rain.* ✓
This mistake has a name: a **dangling participle** (partisip yang 'menggantung', karena tidak menempel pada pelaku yang benar). Native speakers often find it funny, so it's worth checking every time.

id.text:
Klausa partisip tidak punya subjek, jadi bahasa Inggris mengambil subjek dari klausa utama: **kata benda atau kata ganti pertama setelah koma** harus orang yang melakukan kegiatan -ing itu. (**Subjek** = siapa yang melakukan, misalnya *I, Rina, the rain*.)
- *Walking home, **I** got caught in the rain.* ✓ (saya yang berjalan)
- *Walking home, **the rain** started.* ✗ Kalimat ini berarti **hujannya** yang berjalan pulang!
Kalau pelakunya berbeda, pakai klausa lengkap: *As I was walking home, it started to rain.* ✓
Kesalahan ini punya nama: **dangling participle** (partisip yang 'menggantung', karena tidak menempel pada pelaku yang benar). Penutur asli sering menganggapnya lucu, jadi selalu periksa.

rows.en: Walking home, I got caught in the rain.
As I was walking home, it started to rain.
rows.id: Saat saya berjalan pulang, hujan mulai turun.

blocks.text: **Indonesian trap:** Indonesian is relaxed about this. Many people write *Setelah membaca surat itu, hatinya sedih* or *Sambil berjalan pulang, hujan turun*, and everyone understands. In English, translate it word by word and you get a dangling participle. Ask yourself: **who was walking? Is that person right after the comma?** If not, change the main clause (*…, I got caught in the rain*) or use a full clause (*As I was walking home, …*).

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** bahasa Indonesia cukup longgar soal ini. Banyak orang menulis *Setelah membaca surat itu, hatinya sedih* atau *Sambil berjalan pulang, hujan turun*, dan semua orang paham. Kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata ke bahasa Inggris, hasilnya dangling participle. Tanya dirimu: **siapa yang berjalan? Apakah orang itu ada tepat setelah koma?** Kalau tidak, ubah klausa utamanya (*…, I got caught in the rain*) atau pakai klausa lengkap (*As I was walking home, …*).

options: Sitting in the meeting, my phone rang three times.
Sitting in the meeting, I felt my phone ring three times.
blocks.explain: The person sitting in the meeting is 'I', so 'I' must come right after the comma. The first sentence says the phone was sitting in the meeting.

id.explain: Yang duduk dalam rapat adalah 'I', jadi 'I' harus ada tepat setelah koma. Kalimat pertama berarti HP-nya yang duduk dalam rapat.

blocks.text:
When the subject **receives** the action (it is done TO it), start with the **third form (V3)**. The meaning is **passive**, like the passive you know: *The bridge **was built** in 1990. It is still strong.* → ***Built** in 1990, the bridge is still strong.*
A quick map from Indonesian:
- **-ing** ≈ **me-**: the subject **does** it (*Membawa tas besar, Rina naik KRL* → *Carrying a big bag, Rina got on the KRL*).
- **V3** ≈ **di-**: the subject **receives** it (*Dibangun tahun 1990, …* → *Built in 1990, …*).
We call it an '-ed clause' because regular verbs end in -ed (*designed, located, painted*), but irregular verbs use their own V3: *built, made, written, sold, taken*.
**Common mistake:** Indonesian verbs don't change form, so learners write the base form: *'**Build** in 1990, the bridge …'* ✗ → ***Built*** ✓. Not the past simple either: *'**Took** in 2019, the photo …'* ✗ → ***Taken*** ✓.
The subject rule still applies: *'Built in 1990, **we** still use the bridge'* ✗ (we weren't built in 1990!) → *Built in 1990, **the bridge** is still in use.* ✓

id.text:
Kalau subjek **dikenai** tindakan, awali dengan **bentuk ketiga (V3)**. Artinya **pasif**, seperti kalimat pasif yang sudah kamu kenal: *The bridge **was built** in 1990. It is still strong.* → ***Built** in 1990, the bridge is still strong.*
Peta cepat dari bahasa Indonesia:
- **-ing** ≈ **me-**: subjek **melakukan** (*Membawa tas besar, Rina naik KRL* → *Carrying a big bag, Rina got on the KRL*).
- **V3** ≈ **di-**: subjek **dikenai** tindakan (*Dibangun tahun 1990, …* → *Built in 1990, …*).
Namanya '-ed clause' karena kata kerja beraturan berakhiran -ed (*designed, located, painted*), tapi kata kerja tidak beraturan memakai V3-nya sendiri: *built, made, written, sold, taken*.
**Kesalahan umum:** kata kerja bahasa Indonesia tidak berubah bentuk, jadi banyak yang menulis bentuk dasar: *'**Build** in 1990, the bridge …'* ✗ → ***Built*** ✓. Bukan juga bentuk lampau (V2): *'**Took** in 2019, the photo …'* ✗ → ***Taken*** ✓.
Aturan subjek tetap berlaku: *'Built in 1990, **we** still use the bridge'* ✗ (kita tidak dibangun tahun 1990!) → *Built in 1990, **the bridge** is still in use.* ✓

material.title: having + V3 and after + -ing: what happened first

blocks.text:
To show that one action was **finished before** the next one, use **having + V3**: ***Having finished** the report, I went home.* (= After I had finished the report, I went home.) It's very common when the first action took some time: *Having lived in Surabaya for ten years, Pak Hasan knows the city well.*
Another way you met at B1: **after / before / when / while + -ing**. A word like *after* is followed by the -ing form, **never the base form**:
- ***After finishing** the report, I went home.* ✓ (*'After finish'* ✗, *'After finished'* ✗)
- ***Before leaving** the office, please turn off the AC.* ✓
- ***When using** the MRT, have your card ready.* ✓
*Having finished the report, …* and *After finishing the report, …* mean the same, so pick either. And in speech, the full clause is the most natural: *After I finished the report, I went home.*
**Negative:** *Not having received a reply, Bu Ani called the supplier.*

id.text:
Untuk menunjukkan bahwa satu kegiatan **sudah selesai sebelum** kegiatan berikutnya, pakai **having + V3**: ***Having finished** the report, I went home.* (= After I had finished the report, I went home.) Bentuk ini sangat sering dipakai kalau kegiatan pertama makan waktu: *Having lived in Surabaya for ten years, Pak Hasan knows the city well.*
Cara lain yang sudah kamu temui di B1: **after / before / when / while + -ing**. Setelah kata seperti *after*, kata kerjanya memakai bentuk -ing, **bukan bentuk dasar**:
- ***After finishing** the report, I went home.* ✓ (*'After finish'* ✗, *'After finished'* ✗)
- ***Before leaving** the office, please turn off the AC.* ✓
- ***When using** the MRT, have your card ready.* ✓
*Having finished the report, …* dan *After finishing the report, …* artinya sama, jadi pilih salah satu. Saat bicara, klausa lengkap paling wajar: *After I finished the report, I went home.*
**Bentuk negatif:** *Not having received a reply, Bu Ani called the supplier.*

blocks.text: Don't worry about choosing between **-ing** and **having + V3** for every sentence. For two quick actions, one right after the other, plain -ing is also fine: *Opening the email, Rina saw the bad news.* Use **having + V3** when you want to make it clear that the first action was **completely finished** before the second.

id.text: Tidak perlu pusing memilih antara **-ing** dan **having + V3** di setiap kalimat. Untuk dua kegiatan cepat yang langsung berurutan, -ing biasa juga boleh: *Opening the email, Rina saw the bad news.* Pakai **having + V3** kalau kamu ingin menegaskan bahwa kegiatan pertama **benar-benar selesai** sebelum kegiatan kedua.

options: After submit the form, you will get an email.
After submitting the form, you will get an email.
After submitted the form, you will get an email.
blocks.explain: after is followed by the -ing form: after submitting. The base form (submit) and the V3 (submitted) can't follow after without a subject.

id.explain: Setelah after, pakai bentuk -ing: after submitting. Bentuk dasar (submit) dan V3 (submitted) tidak bisa langsung mengikuti after tanpa subjek.

id.title: having + V3 dan after + -ing: apa yang terjadi lebih dulu

suggestedQuestions: Why is 'Walking home, the rain started' wrong?
Do people really use participle clauses when they speak?
How do I know whether to use -ing or the V3?
What's the difference between 'Having finished' and 'After finishing'?

resources.title: Participle clauses
resources.note: A clear explanation of -ing, V3 and having + V3 clauses, the same-subject rule and after/before + -ing, with two grammar tests. The page is marked C1, so some examples (results, conditions) go a little beyond this lesson.

id.note: Penjelasan yang jelas tentang klausa -ing, V3 dan having + V3, aturan subjek yang sama, serta after/before + -ing, dengan dua tes grammar. Halaman ini bertanda C1, jadi beberapa contohnya (hasil, syarat) sedikit melampaui pelajaran ini.

resources.title: Participle clauses: BBC English Class
resources.note: A short (3-minute) video about participle clauses that give a reason, including having + V3. It also uses 'Being …', which this lesson doesn't teach.

id.note: Video pendek (3 menit) tentang klausa partisip yang memberi alasan, termasuk having + V3. Video ini juga memakai 'Being …', yang tidak diajarkan di pelajaran ini.

resources.title: Advanced English Grammar: Participles
resources.note: A longer (14-minute) lesson on using participles in academic and work writing, with complex examples. Above this lesson's level: good if you write essays or reports.

id.note: Pelajaran yang lebih panjang (14 menit) tentang memakai partisip dalam tulisan akademik dan kantor, dengan contoh yang rumit. Di atas level pelajaran ini: cocok kalau kamu menulis esai atau laporan.

id.intro: Hai! Di pelajaran sebelumnya kamu meringkas klausa: the man standing there, the report written by Rina. Hari ini kamu memakai bentuk -ing dan V3 yang sama di awal kalimat untuk menulis kalimat yang lebih ringkas dan lancar: Walking home, I saw Rina. Built in 1990, the bridge is still strong. Having finished the report, I went home. Pemanasan: apa yang salah dengan 'Walking home, the rain started'?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'Walking home, the rain started' salah?
Apakah orang benar-benar memakai klausa partisip saat bicara?
Bagaimana aku tahu kapan pakai -ing dan kapan pakai V3?

assessment.pcl-1: Lengkapi dengan satu kata yang dibentuk dari kata kerja dalam kurung: ___ (wait) for the bus, Budi read the news on his phone.
assessment.pcl-2:
Kalimat mana yang benar? Tulis A atau B.
A: Driving to Bandung, the traffic on the toll road was terrible.
B: Driving to Bandung, we got stuck in terrible traffic on the toll road.
assessment.pcl-3: Buat kalimat ini lebih ringkas dengan klausa -ing, dengan arti yang sama (dalam bahasa Inggris): Because she felt nervous, Sari practised her presentation five times.
assessment.pcl-4: Lengkapi dengan satu kata yang dibentuk dari kata kerja dalam kurung: ___ (write) in 1980, the novel is still popular with students today.
assessment.pcl-5:
Ada satu kata yang salah dalam kalimat ini. Tulis kata yang benar.
Make from recycled plastic, these shopping bags are surprisingly strong.
assessment.pcl-6: Lengkapi dengan having + kata kerja dalam kurung: ___ (finish) her degree in Yogyakarta, Rina moved to Jakarta to work for a startup.
assessment.pcl-7:
Ada satu kata yang salah dalam kalimat ini. Tulis kata yang benar.
After check the figures twice, Pak Hasan sent the report to the directors.
